findings.title: Non-atomic spool drain can lose concurrent receipts or duplicate already-appended receipts
findings.where: src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:74 reads the live spool, src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:94 appends the snapshot to the receipt log, and src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:102 later truncates the same live spool; src/lib/adoption-spool.test.ts:39 covers only a quiescent producer.
findings.what: A hook append occurring after the stream reaches EOF but before line 102 is erased by the truncation and never reaches the canonical log. Separately, if the destination append at lines 94-97 succeeds but truncation at line 102 fails, the catch leaves the original spool intact; retrying drains the same records again. Both outcomes corrupt adoption history and derived scorecard counts.
findings.fix: Serialize drainers and atomically rotate the live spool to a private snapshot before parsing. Immediately recreate the live append target so new hook writes are preserved, drain only the rotated snapshot, and retire that snapshot after successful append using an idempotent recovery protocol that cannot replay a snapshot whose destination append already committed.
findings.acceptance: Add deterministic tests with barriers around EOF, destination append, and snapshot retirement: a receipt appended during a drain remains queued and appears exactly once after the next drain; an injected failure after destination append followed by retry also leaves every receipt exactly once in the canonical log.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:74-106 and src/lib/adoption-spool.test.ts:39-90 at the immutable baseline. There is no lock, rename/snapshot step, append commit marker, or concurrency/failure test that closes either interval; the catch explicitly preserves the spool even when truncation fails after a successful destination append.
